Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Method 3 Scoring 3.1 Strategy Objective You will be placing cards in a 5x5 grid. Each row and column will be compared against your competitors. For each row and column, the player with the best hand will score 1 or 2 points. Method On your turn, either: Place the face-up card on your grid, then flip another 'top' card, or Select another 'top' card, causing it to flip, then place it on your grid Cards can only be placed if they are beside another card (up/down, left/right or touching a corner). The front face of the card will always be one of the colours and numbers shown on the back of the card. This will help you try to get a desired card. Scoring The better combination of cards on each row/column will beat competitors combinations. Cards can be IN ANY ORDER. Combinations from Best to Worst are: Combination Example Example Score Straight Flush 1 2 3 4 5 5 Consecutive numbers (in any order) all in the same colour 2 5 of a Kind 4 4 4 4 4 5 of the same number (any colours) 2 4 of a Kind 4 4 4 4 4 of the same number (any colours) 1 Full House 4 4 4 7 7 3 of a Kind and a Pair (any order, any colours) 1 Straight 1 2 3 4 5 5 Consecutive Numbers (in any order) 1 Flush 4 7 9 2 3 All cards same colour (any numbers) 1 3 of a Kind 4 4 4 3 of the same number (any colours) 1 2 Pairs 4 4 7 7 2 pairs of cards, each with the same number (any colours) 1 Cocktail 4 7 9 2 2 5 different colours (any numbers) 1 1 Pair 4 4 2 cards with the same number (any colours) 1 Strategy Look at the back of cards to find ones that will help your combinations Take cards that your opponent wants If an opponent's row/column is unbeatable, use that row/column as a 'trash can' for your worthless cards Board Game Arena would like to thank Spot Games for making it possible to have this game here. 1861 oneohone العربية беларуская мова български език Brezhoneg Català čeština Dansk Deutsch Ελληνικά English Español Eesti keel فارسی Suomi Français Galego עברית Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Bahasa Indonesia 日本語 한국어 Lietuvių Latviešu Bahasa Malaysia Nederlands Norsk Polski Português Română Русский язык Slovenčina Slovenščina Српски Svenska ไทย Türkçe Українська мова Tiếng Việt 中文 (漢) 中文 (汉) Application loading... ... {DISPLAY_IN_OTHER_LANG} {LANG_REDIRECT_CODE} boardgamearena.com Top Help What is Board Game Arena? [Rating: 2/10] Numbers game with some semi-hidden information and deduction. Not my type of game, won't be replaying.

[Rating: 3/10] Fuh, ez rettenetesen ötlettelen lett, 5x5-ös elrendezésben sorokat oszlopokat kell lepontozni, és a szokásos pókerszerű kombinációk érnek pontokat, régen játszottam ennyire felejthető darabbal.

[Rating: 3/10] Rating based on 10+ online plays.  I wanted to enjoy this, but feels just frustratingly "scripted". Games seem to turn into an exercise where both players try to complete a grid that has nothing but five-of-a-kind on one axis and royal flush on another. Neither player is interested in hate drafting (or doing anything else to hurt the other player), because that would automatically also spoil your own grid. There may be situations where you could hurt yourself just a little less than your move would hurt your opponent, but those seem to be rare occurrences and potentially foiled by bad luck - e

[Rating: 4/10] 4 based on BGG's description of a 4 rating. Played on BGA, 1 game. I believe if I played more than three games this would go way down in rating for me.   There's technically a game here, but just barely in terms of any strategic decisions. I did have a couple of moments in one play that I had a "this is light and fun flipping cards" reflection, but the other 80% of the game I was ready for it to be over.  Probably won't play again and just leave it at a 4 and move on.
